title: Grandpa Has Told This Story 998 TIMES
premise: In a river town where any story told a thousand times happens exactly the way its thousandth telling ends, I find my grandpa telling a story about me to my empty chair every night, eyes shut, and stopping in the middle every time.
twist: Grandpa has never finished the story because the end, and the thousandth telling, are mine to tell. I sit in my chair and tell it with my own ending: I drive home every Sunday to fish with him.
world: A green tackle shop by a wide river: a long pine counter, a wall of bright lures, a wood stove, two worn red armchairs facing each other, one low amber lamp and a chalk slate by the till.
